deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck is reporting on the Washnitzer–Monsky (W.M.) approach to a p-adic cohomology for smooth varieties X_0 over a perfect field k of characteristic p.

Step 1. An arbitrary smooth X_0 cannot be lifted to characteristic 0. W.M. therefore first restrict to affine X_0.

Step 2. By SGA 1, Exp. III (infinitesimal deformation theory of smooth affine schemes: the obstructions lie in H^2 and the classes of liftings in H^1 of coherent sheaves, both of which vanish on an affine scheme), such an X_0 lifts to a smooth formal scheme 𝔛 over S = Spec W(k). The lift is unique up to isomorphism, but the isomorphism is not unique. Concretely, 𝔛 is the limit of smooth liftings X_n over W_n = W_n(k).

Step 3. The naive idea is to take the p-adically completed de Rham complex Ω•_{𝔛/S} = lim Ω•_{X_n/W_n} and set H(X_0) = ℍ*(𝔛, Ω•_{𝔛/S}). Since 𝔛 is affine, coherent sheaves have no higher cohomology, so this equals H*(Γ(𝔛, Ω•)).

Step 4. Grothendieck then shows that this is 'a monster, much bigger than what is needed', using the affine line X_0 = Spec k[t]. There 𝔛 = Specf W{t}, where W{t} = lim W_n[t] is the ring of restricted power series (coefficients a_i → 0 p-adically). The computation is completed on the next page:
- H^1 = W{t}/{f'}.
- A series Σ a_n t^n is the derivative of a restricted series exactly when v_p(a_n) − v_p(n+1) → ∞.
- Since v_p(n+1) is unbounded, the condition a_n → 0 alone does not suffice.
- Hence H^1 has infinite rank over W, not just torsion. For example, Σ p^k t^{p^k−1} is a non-torsion class.

This is the standard motivation for replacing W{t} by the weakly complete ('dagger', overconvergent) algebra W[t]^†, i.e. Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology (Monsky–Washnitzer 1968). The page belongs to Grothendieck's 1967 survey notes ('laïus') on crystals, contrasting W.M. with crystalline cohomology.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The claims check out: smooth affine schemes lift to formal smooth schemes, uniquely up to non-unique isomorphism; ℍ* reduces to cohomology of global sections on an affine formal scheme; the affine-line example yields a huge H^1, as verified on the next page.
Minor imprecision: the reference 'SGA 1960/61, III' is SGA 1, Exposé III.

ideas.what: A smooth affine variety in char p lifts to a smooth formal scheme over W(k), unique up to non-unique isomorphism.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting of smooth affine schemes (Elkik; Grothendieck SGA 1 III)

ideas.what: The de Rham cohomology of the p-adically completed lift is far too large; for the affine line H^1 has infinite rank because integration introduces denominators n+1.
ideas.modern_name: Motivation for weak completion / overconvergent (dagger) algebras in Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology
ideas.where_published: Possibly echoed in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); the example itself is standard in Monsky–Washnitzer and later expositions

deep.surprise_reason: This is Grothendieck's expository account of the well-known Monsky–Washnitzer motivation, namely that the p-adic completion gives too large a de Rham cohomology. It is historically nice as a witness of how Grothendieck learned and presented W.M. in 1967, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Mais on montre que c'est un monstre' is more likely 'Mais montrons que c'est un monstre bien plus gros que ce qu'il faut'.
'On constate trouve en effet que' is likely 'On constatera en effet que' (or 'On trouvera').
The final displayed formula reads ℍ^1(𝔛, Ω•_{𝔛/S}) = ... (superscript 1, continued on the next page).
'(SGA 1960/61, III)' refers to SGA 1, Exposé III.
